name: Stack Pass from Carni
summary: Passing after Carni requires releasing the shoulder-lock connection before clearing the guard and establishing a top pin.
description: Passing after Carni requires shoulder release before clearing the guard. Keep a safe base and avoid forcing either the captured arm or the partner into a neck stack.
overview:
The top player faces a bottom guard player using Carni; the head, shoulder or arm may still be enclosed. Do not drive into a loaded shoulder lock or stack the partner's neck. The instructional priority is arm and head-side-leg clearance, not a leg-lock escape.

A leg clearing the head with an overhook is an upper-body trap, even if a butterfly hook remains below. Avoid reaching away while the opponent sets the triceps control. Keep a balanced base and early inside frames; tap instead of moving against a completed choke or joint lock.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Richie Martinez — Carni shoulder lock from Z guard](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iClQ2Np-n30).

flashcards.question: Stack Pass from Carni (top): Which control has priority before any passing pressure?
flashcards.answer: Clear the shoulder clamp first; the route name does not authorize driving into a loaded Carni.
flashcards.answer_line: Shoulder held by leg and triceps

plausible: Only wrist below retained upper arm
Only the lower hook around your leg
trap: Only head above the opponent's frame

flashcards.question: Stack Pass from Carni (top): Where should the elbow stay before the triceps grip settles?
flashcards.answer: Avoid reaching away into the developing triceps control before the shoulder is clamped.

plausible: Straight past their shoulder
Behind your hips as you turn away
trap: High above head with wrist pinned

flashcards.question: Stack Pass from Carni (top): What is the useful early response before the shoulder lock closes?
flashcards.answer: Work through available inside space with balanced support before the shoulder connection becomes a completed lock.
flashcards.answer_line: Inside frames with a stable base

plausible: Chest lift with elbow outside frame
Wide floor post without inside frame
trap: Wrist grip with chest gap still open

flashcards.question: Stack Pass from Carni (top): Your torso circles while the captured elbow stays behind; what loads?
flashcards.answer: Keep head, torso and captured upper arm aligned while opening space at the hip and thigh. Circling the torso while the elbow stays behind can rotate the retained shoulder; use actual release before turning.
flashcards.answer_line: Shoulder turns against the held arm

plausible: Elbow slips in as chest passes
Triceps grip opens before turn
trap: Low hook turns; upper arm stays free

flashcards.question: Stack Pass from Carni (top): What permits shoulder and elbow extraction?
flashcards.answer: Withdraw the shoulder and elbow after the upper-body enclosure releases, not by forcing posture or circling through it.
flashcards.answer_line: Head-side leg and arm clamp open

plausible: Only their foot loses mat contact
Only hips move beyond one knee
trap: Only their pull on your head stops

flashcards.question: Stack Pass from Carni (top): What establishes side control after the shoulder releases?
flashcards.answer: After complete shoulder release, separately clear the legs and settle balanced chest contact in side control.
flashcards.answer_line: Legs clear; chest beside their torso

plausible: Lift head between both knees
Near knee clear; a leg hook stays in
trap: Knees passed with gap beside chest

flashcards.question: Stack Pass from Carni (top): Why is a lower-leg escape alone insufficient here?
flashcards.answer: The initial problem is a Carni shoulder trap, not a Saddle or ankle entanglement. Freeing a lower leg does not solve it.
flashcards.answer_line: Shoulder remains held by upper clamp

plausible: Only the low hook holds the shoulder
Calf withdrawal frees the upper arm

defender.name: Stack Pass from Carni Defender
defender.description: Stack Pass from Carni (defender): Use the guard and shoulder connection to bring the opponent close before moving the high leg. Manage the shoulder and neck line with a forearm frame as the leg clears the head.
defender.overview:
The top player faces a bottom guard player using Carni; the head, shoulder or arm may still be enclosed. Do not drive into a loaded shoulder lock or stack the partner's neck. The instructional priority is arm and head-side-leg clearance, not a leg-lock escape.

Use the guard and shoulder connection to bring the opponent close before moving the high leg. Manage the shoulder and neck line with a forearm frame as the leg clears the head. Turn partly belly down with the knee close and foot supported rather than wrenching the leg across the head.

Keep the captured arm connected so the opponent cannot freely roll or withdraw the shoulder. Hold the wrist and elbow at a comfortable angle; a small change can load the shoulder rapidly. Release the wrist and leg clamp immediately on a tap or when the partner needs to roll safely.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Once Carni is released, make a guard recovery with inside frames and hip movement before the passer closes the space at your ribs. The old shoulder grip must be let go before you turn or bring the knee shield back.
key_principles: Set the upper-body angle: Use the guard and shoulder connection to bring the opponent close before moving the high leg.
Frame before clearing: Manage the shoulder and neck line with a forearm frame as the leg clears the head.
Anchor through the hips: Turn partly belly down with the knee close and foot supported rather than wrenching the leg across the head.
Hold the triceps: Keep the captured arm connected so the opponent cannot freely roll or withdraw the shoulder.
Control before finishing: Hold the wrist and elbow at a comfortable angle; a small change can load the shoulder rapidly.
Let the lock go: Release the wrist and leg clamp immediately on a tap or when the partner needs to roll safely.

flashcards.question: Stack Pass from Carni (bottom): What retains the shoulder before the opponent can posture?
flashcards.answer: The close knee and upper-arm connection retain the shoulder; do not substitute extra torque for lost control.
flashcards.answer_line: Close knee and retained upper arm

plausible: Wrist held while upper arm slips out
Foot high with knee far away
trap: Knee close with upper-arm grip gone

flashcards.question: Stack Pass from Carni (bottom): Where does the forearm preserve room against forward pressure?
flashcards.answer: Use the inside neck-side frame to manage incoming chest pressure during the leg arrangement.
flashcards.answer_line: Inside on the neck and shoulder

plausible: Outside chest with wrist folded
At near wrist below shoulder line
trap: Behind upper arm with elbow outside

flashcards.question: Stack Pass from Carni (bottom): Which anchor supports the clamp without hauling the foot?
flashcards.answer: The supported foot and close knee work with the hip angle; do not force the position by pulling against the knee.
flashcards.answer_line: Belly down a bit; knee in, foot down

plausible: Flat hips with raised knee wide
Knee fixed; foot pulled across head
trap: Knee close with foot off the mat

flashcards.question: Stack Pass from Carni (bottom): The shoulder connection is gone; what should you recover first?
flashcards.answer: Release the old shoulder grip and use frames plus hip movement to restore a knee barrier before the passer fills the space.
flashcards.answer_line: Release grip, frame, recover a knee

plausible: Chase free wrist with arms reaching
Hold loose arm with both knees out
